headline: Ramayana's tickets are expected to climb toward 90.4K by 9–10 PM, with Diwali tomorrow lifting all three films.
bullets: Namit Malhotra's Ramayana: today is projected at 1.32M tickets (range 1.17M–1.48M), so far 606K, and the 7–8 PM hour is expected at 72.8K (range 57.1K–88.7K). The busiest hour ahead is 9–10 PM at about 90.4K (range 65.1K–117K), and the film is running -1% against yesterday. Its 9.3/10 BookMyShow rating and 7.8/10 critics average lean the forecast up by 10%, while mixed word of mouth adds 0%.

Aadarsha Kutumbam: today is projected at 27.5K (range 24.3K–30.9K), so far 11.9K, and it peaks at 2.3K in the 6–7 PM hour (range 1.9K–2.7K), 37% above yesterday. Review and word-of-mouth information is only collected for films that are switched on, so this forecast is not nudged by signals.

Jailer 2: today is projected at 26.5K (range 23.4K–29.8K), so far 14.3K, and its busiest hour ahead is 9–10 PM at about 1.7K (range 1.2K–2.2K), 9% above yesterday. Review and word-of-mouth information is only collected for films that are switched on, so this forecast is not nudged by signals.

Tomorrow, Sunday 8 Nov, is a Diwali holiday and a strong weekend day. Ramayana is projected at 1.53M (range 1.21M–1.81M), Aadarsha Kutumbam at 28.9K (range 22.8K–34.4K), and Jailer 2 at 27.9K (range 22K–33.1K). The Diwali uplift is an assumption.
watch: Ramayana's signal-based lean could shift as reviews and ratings update, since the nudge fades in over the first hours.
Diwali's effect on Sunday is assumed rather than tested, so the Sunday projections for all three films could move within their stated ranges.
